title: Condition on paragraph rates before interpreting long symbol gaps
statement: On the matched public layout at expected hit rate 0.124, independent hits with changing page rates gave 64/64 long-band rejections with a global null and 2/64 with page centering and fixed page counts. Independent hits with changing paragraph rates and the same expected page mean gave 40/64 long-band rejections with the page-count null and 3/64 when paragraph counts were fixed on the same page statistic. At rate 0.036 and gap-copy probability 0.30, the separately declared lag-20 statistic detects recurrence in 64/64 books with a page statistic and fixed paragraph counts, and 42/64 books when the lag pairs stay within paragraph runs. The broad 11–40 band detects it in only 7/64 and 3/64 respectively. On the paired public transcriptions, the within-paragraph 1–5 average for EVA o exceeded the intact-word shuffle in both editions (ZL p = 0.01, IT p = 0.02). The EVA r lag-20 result against the same word null changed from p = 0.01 and 0.04 with page pairs to p = 0.28 and 0.33 with paragraph pairs. Eligible lag-20 pairs fell from 445 and 444 to 55 and 57. The transliterations are paired readings of the same pages.
check: Implement a public practice measurement of the mean 1–5 lag correlation for EVA o within paragraph runs, with the intact-word permutation null preserving run order. Match both paired practice estimates and the published synthetic calibration before proposing a single hidden-page fact. Keep point lag 20 for r as a separate measurement with explicit eligible-pair and power requirements.

design.data: Public practice only. No uncertain or unmatched paragraph lines. Gaps count ASCII EVA character positions, including intervening spaces. Run boundaries also break at omitted P lines, and the page statistic retains pairs between the recorded runs.
design.sampling: Condition on counts and choose uniform eligible non-space slots within the total, page or paragraph-run scope. Recompute the centered or pooled statistic after each draw. The word-order comparison retains whole observed words and the original run order.
design.test_scope: The rates 0.124 and 0.036 are sensitivity checks near the observed o and r frequencies. Observational probabilities are descriptive per symbol and band. Misses in the simulator define limitations of the specific tests and alternatives.
